k_dyes.name: Dyes from plants
k_dyes.desc: Many plants give colour: beets and madder red, onion skins yellow, woad blue.
k_dyes.topic: Many plants give colour: beets and madder red, onion skins yellow, woad blue; the plant is boiled in water, then yarn is soaked in the dye bath; a fixing step (mordant) makes the colour stay.
k_dyes.page: Many plants give colour: madder roots and beets make red, onion skins make yellow, and woad makes blue. You boil the plant in water to make a dye bath, then soak the yarn in it. Adding a fixer, called a mordant, makes the colour stay.

questions.q: Which plant gives a blue dye?
questions.why: Woad leaves make a blue dye.

questions.q: You want yellow yarn. What should you boil?
questions.why: Onion skins make a warm yellow dye.

questions.q: Your dyed yarn faded when washed. What did you forget?
questions.why: A mordant fixes the dye, so the colour stays when washed.

k_colour_mixing.name: Mixing colours
k_colour_mixing.desc: Primary dye colours red, yellow and blue mix into secondary colours: red + yellow = orange, yellow + blue = green, red + blue = purple.
k_colour_mixing.topic: Primary dye colours red, yellow and blue mix into secondary colours: red + yellow = orange, yellow + blue = green, red + blue = purple; mixing all three makes brown.
k_colour_mixing.page: Red, yellow and blue are the main dye colours. Mix two of them to make a new colour. Red and yellow make orange, yellow and blue make green, and red and blue make purple. Mix all three together and you get brown.

questions.q: Which two dye colours make green?
questions.why: Yellow mixed with blue gives green.

questions.q: You mix red and blue dye. What colour do you get?
questions.why: Red and blue together make purple.

questions.q: You pour red, yellow and blue together. What colour now?
questions.why: Mixing all three main colours makes brown.

k_worms.name: Worms make soil
k_worms.desc: Earthworms eat dead leaves and compost and leave behind castings, the richest soil food.
k_worms.topic: Earthworms eat dead leaves and compost and leave behind castings, the richest soil food; their tunnels let air and water into the soil; a worm bin turns kitchen scraps into castings.
k_worms.page: Earthworms eat dead leaves and compost. What they leave behind is called castings, and it is the richest food for soil. Their tunnels let air and water into the ground. In a worm bin, worms turn kitchen scraps into castings.

questions.q: What are worm castings?
answers: What worms leave behind after eating
Little worm eggs in the soil
questions.why: Castings are worm droppings, and they are very rich food for plants.

questions.q: How do worm tunnels help your plants?
answers: They let air and water in
They catch the slugs at night
questions.why: Tunnels make paths for air and water to reach the roots.

questions.q: What does a worm bin do with kitchen scraps?
questions.why: Worms eat the scraps and leave castings, a rich food for soil.

k_seed_saving.name: Saving seeds
k_seed_saving.desc: Heirloom plants grow true from their own seeds: let the best plants flower, collect the dry seeds, keep them cool and dry for next year.
k_seed_saving.topic: Heirloom plants grow true from their own seeds: let the best plants flower, collect the dry seeds, keep them cool and dry for next year; seed libraries share old varieties so they don't disappear.
k_seed_saving.page: Heirloom plants are old kinds that grow true from their own seeds: the new plants come out just like the parent. Let your best plants flower, and collect the seeds when they are dry. Keep them cool and dry until next year. Seed libraries share old kinds of seeds, so they don't disappear.

questions.q: Which plants should you save seeds from?
questions.why: Seeds from your best plants grow into good plants too.

questions.q: How should you store saved seeds?
questions.why: Cool, dry seeds stay healthy until planting time next year.

questions.q: Why do seed libraries share old seeds?
answers: So old seeds can be thrown away
questions.why: When many people grow old kinds, those plants stay alive for the future.

k_saffron.name: Saffron, the precious spice
k_saffron.desc: Saffron comes from the three red threads (stigmas) inside each crocus flower, picked by hand.
k_saffron.topic: Saffron comes from the three red threads (stigmas) inside each crocus flower, picked by hand; it takes about 150 flowers for one gram, which is why it is so precious; it colours food golden.
k_saffron.page: Saffron comes from a purple crocus flower. Inside each flower are three red threads, called stigmas, and they are picked by hand. It takes about 150 flowers to make just one gram, so saffron is very precious. A pinch colours food a golden yellow.

questions.q: Why does saffron cost so much?
answers: It grows on big, tall trees
questions.why: About 150 flowers, all picked by hand, make just one gram.

questions.q: Which part of the crocus is saffron?
questions.why: Saffron is the three red threads, called stigmas, in each flower.

questions.q: What does a pinch of saffron do to rice?
questions.why: Just a pinch of saffron turns food a golden yellow.

k_master_baking.name: Master baking
k_master_baking.desc: Fine flour is ground twice and sifted for light cakes.
k_master_baking.topic: Fine flour is ground twice and sifted for light cakes; eggs trap air when beaten; butter and sugar creamed together make cakes soft; an even oven temperature bakes the inside before the outside burns.
k_master_baking.page: For light cakes, flour is ground twice and sifted until it is very fine. Beating eggs traps tiny air bubbles. Creaming, or beating, butter and sugar together makes a cake soft. The oven must be evenly hot, not too hot, so the inside bakes before the outside burns.

questions.q: Why beat the eggs for a cake?
answers: To warm them up for the oven
questions.why: Beaten eggs hold air, which makes the cake light.

questions.q: Your cake burned outside but stayed raw inside. Why?
answers: The eggs were beaten too long
questions.why: Steady, gentle heat lets the middle bake before the outside burns.

questions.q: How do you make flour fine enough for light cakes?
answers: Grind it twice and sift it
Mix in plenty of coarse bran
questions.why: Grinding twice and sifting makes very fine flour for light cakes.

k_wind_pump.name: Pumping water with wind
k_wind_pump.desc: A wind pump uses the turning sails to move a pump rod up and down, lifting water from deep underground into a tank, day and night whenever the wind blows — without anyone pumping by hand.
k_wind_pump.topic: A wind pump uses the turning sails to move a pump rod up and down, lifting water from deep underground into a tank, day and night whenever the wind blows — without anyone pumping by hand.
k_wind_pump.page: A wind pump uses its turning sails to move a pump rod up and down. Each stroke lifts water from deep underground into a tank. It works day and night, whenever the wind blows, with nobody pumping by hand.

questions.q: What makes a wind pump work?
questions.why: The wind spins the sails, and that drives the pump.

questions.q: How does a wind pump lift water?
answers: A rod moves up and down
questions.why: The sails move a pump rod up and down, lifting water each time.

questions.q: When does a wind pump fill the tank?
questions.why: It runs whenever there is wind, even at night.

k_living_soil.name: Living soil
k_living_soil.desc: A spoonful of healthy soil holds billions of tiny living things — bacteria, fungi, worms.
k_living_soil.topic: A spoonful of healthy soil holds billions of tiny living things — bacteria, fungi, worms; fungi threads help roots find water; feeding the soil with compost and not digging it too much keeps it alive.
k_living_soil.page: Healthy soil is alive! One spoonful holds billions of tiny living things, like bacteria and fungi, and worms live there too. Fungi grow long, thin threads that help roots find water. Feed the soil with compost and don't dig it too much, and it stays alive.

questions.q: How many tiny living things are in a spoonful of healthy soil?
questions.why: Healthy soil is packed with billions of tiny living things.

questions.q: How do fungi help plant roots?
answers: Their threads help roots find water
They scare away the slugs and snails
questions.why: Long, thin fungus threads reach far and help roots get water.

questions.q: How can you keep your soil alive?
answers: Add compost and dig only a little
Dig it up deeply every single week
questions.why: Compost feeds the soil life, and too much digging disturbs it.
